clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old girl presented with two firm, erythematous, asymptomatic nodules on the left cheek gradually increasing over two months, with no systemic symptoms or lymphadenopathy and no response to initial amoxicillin-clavulanate antibiotic therapy. Clinical examination revealed firm, non-fluctuant nodules with overlying erythematous skin. Microbiological and molecular tests including Ziehl–Neelsen and Gram stains, cultures for bacteria, fungi, acid-fast bacilli, and antibody tests for Bartonella henselae and Afipia felis were negative, supporting an aseptic process. Empiric treatment with topical fusidic acid and oral clarithromycin was started. The lesion resolved completely within two months without recurrence at one month follow-up. Histopathology report confirmation is lacking in the disclosed evidence but clinical features, negative infectious workup, and clinical course with resolution after targeted therapy strongly support the diagnosis of idiopathic facial aseptic granuloma.
